title: Seminuclear Flip Phacoemulsification for Soft Nuclear Cataract Surgery: A New Soft Nucleus Cataract Chopping Technique

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: ali:license_ref https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/; Journal of Ophthalmology, John Wiley & Sons)

indication: Age-related soft nuclear cataract (Emery-Little grade 1-2), age over 50 years, preoperative ECD above 1200 cells/mm2; previous intraocular surgery, corneal disease, glaucoma, uveitis, axial length outside 22-28 mm and zonular weakness excluded

groups.description: Seminuclear flip phacoemulsification (SNFP), the new soft-nucleus chopping technique introduced as the experimental arm; randomized block design stratified by nuclear grade; 2.8 mm temporal clear corneal incision, 5.0-5.5 mm capsulorhexis; single surgeon

Conventional quick-chop phacoemulsification (QCP), the study's control group; randomized block design stratified by nuclear grade; 2.8 mm temporal clear corneal incision, 5.0-5.5 mm capsulorhexis; single surgeon

exclusions.reason: Test statistics and p-values are not admissible

notes: The article introduces SNFP as a new technique and calls QCP the control group (randomized): SNFP is the treated (investigational technique) arm and QCP the control arm (same roles as the endothelium record ecd-pmc13425044).
Two posterior capsule ruptures in the QCP group were managed with anterior vitrectomy and sulcus IOL; their postoperative outcome data were excluded by the authors.
CCT was measured by AS-OCT (Carl Zeiss Meditec); Pentacam AXL was used only for corneal astigmatism (Methods).
